column1: On the Effectiveness of the ECB’s Conventional and Unconventional Policies under Uncertainty

The thesis titled On the Effectiveness of the European Central Bank's Conventional and Unconventional Policies Under Uncertainty by Niko Hauzenberger  Michael Pfarrhofer  and Anna Stelzer from the University of Salzburg examines the impact of the European Central Bank's (ECB) monetary policies in the context of economic uncertainty. The study focuses on both conventional and unconventional monetary policy measures  such as changes in the short-term policy rate  forward guidance  and quantitative easing  and their effectiveness under varying levels of uncertainty in the euro area (EA).

To analyze these effects  the authors employ a Bayesian smooth-transition vector autoregression (ST-VAR) model  which allows them to capture the non-linear dynamics of monetary policy transmission under different uncertainty conditions. The research utilizes high-frequency financial market data to identify exogenous variations in central bank policy around policy announcement dates  enabling the authors to trace the dynamic effects of monetary policy shocks on key macroeconomic and financial variables  as well as survey-based measures of expectations.

The findings of the study indicate that the transmission channels of monetary policy are impaired during periods of elevated uncertainty. Specifically  conventional monetary policy measures  such as adjustments to the policy rate  are found to be less effective in such times. Forward guidance also shows reduced effectiveness under high uncertainty  although to a lesser extent. In contrast  quantitative easing measures appear to maintain their effectiveness even when uncertainty is high  suggesting that unconventional monetary policies may be more robust tools in uncertain economic environments.

The paper contributes to the existing literature by highlighting the importance of considering economic uncertainty as a key determinant of the effectiveness of monetary policy measures. It also underscores the potential limitations of conventional monetary policy tools during periods of heightened uncertainty and the relative resilience of unconventional measures like quantitative easing.

The study acknowledges the support of various funding bodies  including the Austrian Science Fund and the Oesterreichische Nationalbank  and expresses gratitude to individuals who provided valuable comments and suggestions. The research is part of a broader effort to understand the complex interactions between monetary policy and economic conditions  particularly in the context of the euro area  where the ECB plays a crucial role in maintaining economic stability.
